transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon, broadband technical line, my name is Greg.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Greg, my name is Nadia Patel. Our broadband router has started rebooting itself six or seven times an hour: whenever anyone walks past the hallway table or brushes against the power lead, the lights on the router die completely and it takes five minutes to reconnect to the internet!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can inspect your router power supply and line uptime logs. Before we test your connection, could you confirm your full postal address and your account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 83 Victoria Road, Cambridge, CB4 3BW, security PIN 5521, router model S-Net Hub 4.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Nadia, that confirms your account details. Have you inspected the black power adapter plug connected to the rear of the router?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The round barrel plug is loose inside the socket on the back of the hub: if I touch the wire with a single finger, the hub loses power immediately!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could I place you on hold for two minutes while I check your router power and uptime telemetry?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Nadia. The network telemetry confirms forty-two sudden router power loss events over the past twenty-four hours.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you dispatch a replacement twelve-volt power supply adapter to replace this loose one?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Power supply accessories are classified as consumable customer premises equipment and are not covered under free replacement policies.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Not covered?! The router is only five months old! S-Net supplied the power plug!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you place your sensitive broadband router on a wobbly hallway table where people kick the cables, of course the power plug is going to loosen.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No one kicked the cable! It is sitting on a solid console table! Why are you blaming me for a loose factory power connector?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am stating the standard causes of physical strain damage on DC barrel sockets.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So what is your solution for a five-month-old router that keeps losing power?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can order an official S-Net replacement power adapter through our customer shop for thirty-nine pounds ninety-nine.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am not paying forty pounds for a power lead when I pay sixty pounds a month for your service!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is our standard accessory replacement policy for consumer premises hardware.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can I speak with a manager who has the authority to waive a forty-pound power plug charge?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously twelve-volt barrel connectors require a snug mechanical fit into the internal chassis socket.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I know it requires a snug fit! That is why I am asking for a working plug!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Nadia speaking, our internet cuts out every twenty minutes whenever anyone walks past the hall table! I work from home as an intensive care triage dispatcher and my remote database session drops in the middle of emergency bed allocations! It is terrifying and unacceptable that S-Net provides hardware that shuts off at the slightest vibration!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how terrifying and stressful it is to have your connection cut out during intensive care hospital bed allocations, Nadia. Experiencing power loss from slight vibrations is completely unacceptable for mission-critical work, so let us troubleshoot the physical power adapter immediately.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will you dispatch a replacement power adapter today?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: As I advised, frontline agents cannot override accessory dispatch charges without supervisory approval.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Then get supervisory approval right now while I am on the phone!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Team supervisors do not take telephony escalations for power supply accessories.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there any temporary fix I can use to prevent the hub from dying during my shifts?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You could wrap insulating tape around the plastic barrel neck to increase friction inside the socket.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You want an NHS critical care dispatcher to tape a faulty electrical plug with insulating tape?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am offering a practical zero-cost suggestion to prevent lateral movement.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is a fire hazard and an insult. What happens when the hub reboots during an emergency call tonight?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: S-Net cannot accept liability for critical service interruptions on residential consumer contracts.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You pride yourself on reliable broadband in your advertising, but your equipment is falling apart.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our advertising reflects network availability across our external telecommunications infrastructure.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you at least log an official hardware complaint regarding the build quality of the Hub 4 power socket?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can submit a hardware defect feedback form to our quality assurance team.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What is the reference number for that hardware complaint?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The defect feedback tracking reference is DEF-88190-C.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: DEF-88190-C, noted down.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Defect feedback forms are reviewed by product engineering within thirty business days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thirty business days does not help me tonight.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before I document the hardware fault, what model router did you say was on the hall table again?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: As I told you at the start of our call, it is the S-Net Hub 4.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have recorded the Hub 4 model on the hardware defect report.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So the internet will continue cutting out every twenty minutes and S-Net refuses to send a five-pound power lead.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You retain the option to purchase the replacement power adapter via our website.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will be purchasing an adapter from Amazon for eight pounds and submitting the receipt to the Small Claims Court.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is your prerogative as a consumer.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: This has been the most appalling customer service I have ever encountered.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there any other aspect of your broadband connection I can assist you with today, Nadia?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, you have completely failed to resolve my problem.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
